packages.title: Improve local delivery
packages.hypothesis: Coordinating existing capacity and making vaccination access clearer may improve uptake in participating catchments.
actions: Confirm appointment capacity with participating providers
Distribute clear local appointment information through existing channels
Discuss unresolved delivery barriers with local stakeholders
packages.rationale: Access index 35/100 and availability index 48/100 point to delivery conditions worth investigating. Coverage is 50.7%.
packages.primary_metric: Pharmacy-dispensing proxy per 10,000 people aged 65+ in fixed participating catchments
packages.final_decision: Retain the delivery work, resolve the remaining site barrier, and collect administration evidence before attributing uptake gains.
packages.comparator: Matched comparison catchments that are not participating. Matching uses baseline trajectory and relevant characteristics, not cluster membership alone.
packages.footprint_note: Defined participating catchments within the department, not the whole department. Package populations do not overlap.

checkpoints.execution: Baseline: no activity has started yet.
7 of 12 sites active; availability problems delay two sites.
10 sites active; appointment information is consistent, but one locality remains difficult to reach.
11 sites active; one site remains delayed and availability still warrants follow-up.

roles: Market Access coordinates delivery with local providers and partners

packages.title: Strengthen recommendations and follow-through
packages.hypothesis: Where access is available but recommendation and follow-through are weaker, coordinated provider recommendations, community information and reminders may help more eligible older adults complete vaccination.
actions: Medical supports a short briefing for participating pharmacies and practices on proactive recommendations to eligible adults aged 65+.
Public Affairs coordinates existing community partners to share clear information about eligibility and local vaccination access.
Participating providers use their own reminder processes to help eligible adults follow through.
The team records which sites have started the activities and reviews execution and dispensing trends fortnightly.
packages.rationale: Coverage is 46.4%, with a larger gap among adults aged 65–74 than those aged 75+. Access (66) and availability (86) are relatively strong, while provider engagement (34) and recommendation (40) are weak. Local partners should validate this interpretation.
packages.primary_metric: Pharmacy-dispensing proxy per 10,000 people aged 65+ in fixed participating catchments
packages.final_decision: Continue where delivery is established, complete the remaining site, and refine partner messaging or reminder execution. Whether to extend the approach to other Activation-gap departments is a decision for the team.
packages.comparator: Matched comparison catchments that are not participating. Matching uses baseline trajectory and relevant characteristics, not cluster membership alone.
packages.footprint_note: Defined participating catchments within the department, not the whole department. Package populations do not overlap.

checkpoints.execution: Baseline: no activity has started yet.
10 of 20 sites active; outreach is underway but the proxy has not separated from comparison catchments.
17 sites active; an early relative signal has emerged, with uneven partner reach.
19 sites active; directional comparative improvement is present, while one site and some audiences remain under-reached.

roles: Participating providers own recommendations, reminders and vaccination delivery
Market Access supports delivery barriers where relevant
Patient-level reminder data stay with providers

packages.title: Implement the 65+ recommendation
support: Commercial — separate brand and availability investigation
packages.hypothesis: Clearer implementation of the French recommendation may increase enhanced-category adoption; brand performance needs a separate assessment.
actions: Brief participating teams on equivalent HAS positioning of Efluelda and Fluad
Review the local pathway and availability of recommended options
Record questions that prevent consistent implementation
Investigate Efluelda account availability separately through Commercial
packages.rationale: Coverage is 59.3%. Enhanced vaccines account for 40% of observed 65+ flu dispensing at baseline.
packages.primary_metric: Enhanced-vaccine share of observed 65+ flu dispensing (%)
packages.final_decision: Retain useful category education; ask Commercial to investigate product availability and account execution. Category growth alone does not establish a brand-share gain.
packages.comparator: Matched comparison catchments that are not participating. Matching uses baseline trajectory and relevant characteristics, not cluster membership alone.
packages.footprint_note: Defined participating catchments within the department, not the whole department. Package populations do not overlap.

checkpoints.execution: Baseline: no activity has started yet.
9 of 15 sites briefed; both participating and comparison sites show category movement.
13 sites active; category adoption is improving more quickly, while Efluelda share is flat.
14 sites active; category implementation progresses, but Efluelda share within the category remains unchanged.

roles: Medical and Market Access lead recommendation and pathway education
Commercial separately investigates Efluelda availability and account execution

aggregation: For P1/P2 use fixed target-population weighted average of dose-rate changes. Keep P3 share-change separately. No causal attribution.
